passages.text: I will stand at my guard post and station myself on the ramparts. I will watch to see what He will say to me, and how I should answer when corrected.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Habakkuk speaks.
He waits for God’s answer.
He says, “I will stand at my guard post.”
He says, “I will station myself on the ramparts.”
He says, “I will watch to see what God will say to me.”
He says, “I will see how I should answer when God corrects me.”
passages.original: עַל־ מִשְׁמַרְתִּ֣י אֶעֱמֹ֔דָה וְאֶֽתְיַצְּבָ֖ה עַל־ מָצ֑וֹר וַאֲצַפֶּ֗ה לִרְאוֹת֙ מַה־ יְדַבֶּר־ בִּ֔י וּמָ֥ה אָשִׁ֖יב עַל־ תּוֹכַחְתִּֽי׃

passages.text: Then the LORD answered me: “Write down this vision and clearly inscribe it on tablets, so that a herald may run with it.
passages.sermon:
The LORD answered me.
He spoke to me.
He said, “Write down this vision.
Make it clear on tablets.
Do this so a herald can run with it.
The herald will carry the message quickly.
The message will be easy to read and share.”
passages.original: וַיַּעֲנֵ֤נִי יְהוָה֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר כְּת֣וֹב חָז֔וֹן וּבָאֵ֖ר עַל־ הַלֻּח֑וֹת לְמַ֥עַן יָר֖וּץ ק֥וֹרֵא בֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For the vision awaits an appointed time; it testifies of the end and does not lie. Though it lingers, wait for it, since it will surely come and will not delay.
passages.sermon:
God gave a vision.
This vision has a set time.
The vision points to the end.
The vision speaks the truth.
The vision does not lie.
If the vision seems slow, wait for it.
The vision will surely come.
The vision will not delay.
passages.original: כִּ֣י ע֤וֹד חָזוֹן֙ לַמּוֹעֵ֔ד וְיָפֵ֥חַ לַקֵּ֖ץ וְלֹ֣א יְכַזֵּ֑ב אִם־ יִתְמַהְמָהּ֙ חַכֵּה־ ל֔וֹ כִּֽי־ בֹ֥א יָבֹ֖א לֹ֥א יְאַחֵֽר׃

passages.text: Look at the proud one; his soul is not upright — but the righteous will live by faith — and wealth indeed betrays him. He is an arrogant man never at rest. He enlarges his appetite like Sheol, and like Death, he is never satisfied. He gathers all the nations to himself and collects all the peoples as his own.
passages.sermon:
The proud person stands before us.
His soul is not right within him.
He does not live in a way that pleases God.
But the righteous person lives by faith.
The righteous person trusts God and finds life.
Wealth betrays the proud man.
He is arrogant.
He never finds rest.
He opens his desires wide, like the grave.
He is like Death.
He is never satisfied.
He gathers all the nations to himself.
He collects all the peoples as his own.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֣ה עֻפְּלָ֔ה לֹא־ יָשְׁרָ֥ה נַפְשׁ֖וֹ בּ֑וֹ וְצַדִּ֖יק בֶּאֱמוּנָת֥וֹ יִחְיֶֽה׃ וְאַף֙ כִּֽי־ הַיַּ֣יִן בּוֹגֵ֔ד גֶּ֥בֶר יָהִ֖יר וְלֹ֣א יִנְוֶ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֩ הִרְחִ֨יב כִּשְׁא֜וֹל נַפְשׁ֗וֹ וְה֤וּא כַמָּ֙וֶת֙ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׂבָּ֔ע וַיֶּאֱסֹ֤ף אֵלָיו֙ כָּל־ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וַיִּקְבֹּ֥ץ אֵלָ֖יו כָּל־ הָעַמִּֽים׃

passages.text: Will not all of these take up a taunt against him, speaking with mockery and derision: ‘Woe to him who amasses what is not his and makes himself rich with many loans! How long will this go on?’
passages.sermon:
Many people see the proud and greedy man.
They speak against him.
They mock him.
They use riddles and taunts about him.
They say, “Woe to the one who gathers what does not belong to him.
He makes himself rich with many loans.
How long will this continue?”
passages.original: הֲלוֹא־ אֵ֣לֶּה כֻלָּ֗ם עָלָיו֙ מָשָׁ֣ל יִשָּׂ֔אוּ וּמְלִיצָ֖ה חִיד֣וֹת ל֑וֹ וְיֹאמַ֗ר ה֚וֹי הַמַּרְבֶּ֣ה לֹּא־ ל֔וֹ עַד־ מָתַ֕י וּמַכְבִּ֥יד עָלָ֖יו עַבְטִֽיט׃

passages.text: Will not your creditors suddenly arise and those who disturb you awaken? Then you will become their prey.
passages.sermon:
Your creditors will rise up suddenly.
Those who trouble you will wake up.
They will act against you.
You will become prey for them.
passages.original: הֲל֣וֹא פֶ֗תַע יָק֙וּמוּ֙ נֹשְׁכֶ֔יךָ וְיִקְצ֖וּ מְזַעְזְעֶ֑יךָ וְהָיִ֥יתָ לִמְשִׁסּ֖וֹת לָֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: Because you have plundered many nations, the remnant of the people will plunder you— because of your bloodshed against man and your violence against the land, the city, and all their dwellers.
passages.sermon:
You have plundered many nations.
You took what belonged to others.
You acted with violence and greed.
You shed blood among people.
You brought harm to the land.
You hurt the city and everyone living there.
Now, the remnant of the people will plunder you.
They will take from you what you took from others.
They will do this because of your bloodshed and violence.
passages.original: כִּֽי אַתָּ֤ה שַׁלּ֙וֹתָ֙ גּוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֔ים יְשָׁלּ֖וּךָ כָּל־ יֶ֣תֶר עַמִּ֑ים מִדְּמֵ֤י אָדָם֙ וַחֲמַס־ אֶ֔רֶץ קִרְיָ֖ה וְכָל־ יֹ֥שְׁבֵי בָֽהּ׃פ

passages.text: Woe to him who builds his house by unjust gain, to place his nest on high and escape the hand of disaster!
passages.sermon:
God warns people who gain wealth by evil means.
He says, “Woe to the person who gets profit by injustice.”
This person tries to make his house safe by wrongdoing.
He builds his home high up, like a nest on a mountain.
He does this to escape trouble and disaster.
But God sees his actions.
God will judge those who use evil to protect themselves.
passages.original: ה֗וֹי בֹּצֵ֛עַ בֶּ֥צַע רָ֖ע לְבֵית֑וֹ לָשׂ֤וּם בַּמָּרוֹם֙ קִנּ֔וֹ לְהִנָּצֵ֖ל מִכַּף־ רָֽע׃

passages.text: You have plotted shame for your house by cutting off many peoples and forfeiting your life.
passages.sermon:
You have brought shame to your house.
You planned evil.
You destroyed many peoples.
You harmed your own life.
You lost your life because of your actions.
passages.original: יָעַ֥צְתָּ בֹּ֖שֶׁת לְבֵיתֶ֑ךָ קְצוֹת־ עַמִּ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים וְחוֹטֵ֥א נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

passages.text: For the stones will cry out from the wall, and the rafters will echo it from the woodwork.
passages.sermon:
God sees every act of injustice.
He knows when people build their houses by evil gain.
Even if no person speaks, the stones in the wall will cry out.
The wooden beams will answer from the woodwork.
Creation itself will testify against wrongdoing.
passages.original: כִּי־ אֶ֖בֶן מִקִּ֣יר תִּזְעָ֑ק וְכָפִ֖יס מֵעֵ֥ץ יַעֲנֶֽנָּה׃פ

passages.text: Woe to him who builds a city with bloodshed and establishes a town by iniquity!
passages.sermon:
God warns people who do evil.
God sees those who build cities with bloodshed.
God sees those who establish towns with injustice.
God says, “Woe to the person who does these things.”
Bloodshed means killing or harming others.
Iniquity means doing what is wrong or unjust.
God does not bless cities built on violence.
God does not bless towns founded on sin.
passages.original: ה֛וֹי בֹּנֶ֥ה עִ֖יר בְּדָמִ֑ים וְכוֹנֵ֥ן קִרְיָ֖ה בְּעַוְלָֽה׃

passages.text: Is it not indeed from the LORD of Hosts that the labor of the people only feeds the fire, and the nations weary themselves in vain?
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts rules over all.
He causes the people to labor.
Their work only feeds the fire.
The nations strive and grow tired.
Their efforts are in vain.
passages.original: הֲל֣וֹא הִנֵּ֔ה מֵאֵ֖ת יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת וְיִֽיגְע֤וּ עַמִּים֙ בְּדֵי־ אֵ֔שׁ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים בְּדֵי־ רִ֥יק יִעָֽפוּ׃

passages.text: For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD as the waters cover the sea.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is glorious.
The earth will be filled with the knowledge of the LORD’s glory.
This knowledge will spread everywhere.
It will cover the earth completely.
The knowledge will cover the earth like water covers the sea.
passages.original: כִּ֚י תִּמָּלֵ֣א הָאָ֔רֶץ לָדַ֖עַת אֶת־ כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֑ה כַּמַּ֖יִם יְכַסּ֥וּ עַל־ יָֽם׃ס

passages.text: Woe to him who gives drink to his neighbors, pouring it from the wineskin until they are drunk, in order to gaze at their nakedness!
passages.sermon:
God warns people who act with evil intent.
Some people give their neighbors strong drink.
They pour out wine until their neighbors become drunk.
They do this so they can look at their neighbors’ nakedness.
God says woe to such people.
passages.original: ה֚וֹי מַשְׁקֵ֣ה רֵעֵ֔הוּ מְסַפֵּ֥חַ חֲמָתְךָ֖ וְאַ֣ף שַׁכֵּ֑ר לְמַ֥עַן הַבִּ֖יט עַל־ מְעוֹרֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: You will be filled with shame instead of glory. You too must drink and expose your uncircumcision! The cup in the LORD’s right hand will come around to you, and utter disgrace will cover your glory.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God holds power and judgment in His right hand.
You have received shame instead of honor.
You will drink from the cup of the LORD’s judgment.
You will be exposed in your uncleanness.
The cup in the LORD’s right hand will come to you.
Disgrace will cover your former glory.
passages.original: שָׂבַ֤עְתָּ קָלוֹן֙ מִכָּב֔וֹד שְׁתֵ֥ה גַם־ אַ֖תָּה וְהֵֽעָרֵ֑ל תִּסּ֣וֹב עָלֶ֗יךָ כּ֚וֹס יְמִ֣ין יְהוָ֔ה וְקִיקָל֖וֹן עַל־ כְּבוֹדֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: For your violence against Lebanon will overwhelm you, and the destruction of animals will terrify you, because of your bloodshed against men and your violence against the land, the city, and all their dwellers.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to those who have done violence.
You have committed violence against Lebanon.
This violence will overwhelm you.
You have destroyed animals.
This destruction will terrify you.
You have shed blood among people.
You have done violence to the land.
You have harmed the city.
You have harmed all who live in the city.
passages.original: כִּ֣י חֲמַ֤ס לְבָנוֹן֙ יְכַסֶּ֔ךָּ וְשֹׁ֥ד בְּהֵמ֖וֹת יְחִיתַ֑ן מִדְּמֵ֤י אָדָם֙ וַחֲמַס־ אֶ֔רֶץ קִרְיָ֖ה וְכָל־ יֹ֥שְׁבֵי בָֽהּ׃ס

passages.text: What use is an idol, that a craftsman should carve it— or an image, a teacher of lies? For its maker trusts in his own creation; he makes idols that cannot speak.
passages.sermon:
An idol is a statue or image made by a craftsman.
A craftsman carves the idol with his own hands.
The idol is only an object.
The idol cannot help anyone.
The idol cannot speak.
The idol cannot teach truth.
The idol teaches lies.
The craftsman trusts in what he has made.
He puts his hope in his own creation.
He makes idols that are silent and powerless.
passages.original: מָֽה־ הוֹעִ֣יל פֶּ֗סֶל כִּ֤י פְסָלוֹ֙ יֹֽצְר֔וֹ מַסֵּכָ֖ה וּמ֣וֹרֶה שָּׁ֑קֶר כִּ֣י בָטַ֞ח יֹצֵ֤ר יִצְרוֹ֙ עָלָ֔יו לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת אֱלִילִ֥ים אִלְּמִֽים׃ס

passages.text: Woe to him who says to wood, ‘Awake!’ or to silent stone, ‘Arise!’ Can it give guidance? Behold, it is overlaid with gold and silver, yet there is no breath in it at all.”
passages.sermon:
The prophet Habakkuk speaks against idol worship.
He warns people who talk to wood and say, “Awake!”
He warns people who speak to a silent stone and say, “Arise!”
He asks, “Can it give guidance?”
He points out the idol is covered with gold and silver.
He says there is no breath in the idol.
He shows the idol has no life inside it.
passages.original: ה֣וֹי אֹמֵ֤ר לָעֵץ֙ הָקִ֔יצָה ע֖וּרִי לְאֶ֣בֶן דּוּמָ֑ם ה֣וּא יוֹרֶ֔ה הִנֵּה־ ה֗וּא תָּפוּשׂ֙ זָהָ֣ב וָכֶ֔סֶף וְכָל־ ר֖וּחַ אֵ֥ין בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But the LORD is in His holy temple; let all the earth be silent before Him.
passages.sermon: The LORD is present in His holy temple.\r\nThe LORD is holy.\r\nLet all the earth be silent before the LORD.
passages.original: וַֽיהוָ֖ה בְּהֵיכַ֣ל קָדְשׁ֑וֹ הַ֥ס מִפָּנָ֖יו כָּל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃פ
